limitations: Source correspondence only; no independent clinical diagnosis or modern ACMG reassessment.
Packet age64 at last encounter does not match article latest age69/follow-up2016; identity is otherwise secure.
One family, incomplete penetrance, P4 uncertain WD ascertainment, and unexcluded modifier effects qualify causal certainty.
Original genome assembly/transcript remapping not independently performed; source numeric coordinate and coding/protein call agree.

patient_identity.statement: Patient1 maps securely to female proband P1=IV.6, daughter of P3=III.4, with recurrent right-knee arthritis and positive joint-fluid Tw. However packet age64 at last encounter conflicts with article description as69 and follow-up2016 (birth1948 implies about68 then). Age64 could represent an earlier undocumented extraction time, not the reported latest encounter. Young-adult onset is compatible with arthritis since1980, about32years; diagnosis in2011 is later.

evidence.locator: Results multiplex kindred; Patients and family lines119-128; Figure1A; source-data1 row11

limitations: Mismatch concerns age chronology, not which patient; the article itself uses a later age snapshot than its2016 follow-up.

genotype.statement: Source reports heterozygous IRF4 exon3 c.292C>T, p.Arg98Trp/R98W, with C/T Sanger trace for P1. Source-data Figure1-data2 row2 lists chr6:394896 C>T, numerically matching packet. Source resource transcript is NM_002460.3 and WES uses hg19; packet names NM_002460.4 and NC_000006.12/hg38.

evidence.locator: Figure1B-C; Results private heterozygous variant; Materials genome-wide analysis; key-resource table; Figure1-data2 row2

limitations: Coding/protein/zygosity and numeric position correspondence established; independent version/assembly normalization not performed.

segregation.statement: P1 and her affected father P3 are WT/R98W, mother III.5 WT/WT; pedigree and source table support paternal inheritance. All four designated patients and eight additional relatives carry R98W; five healthy carriers are Tw-positive, two negative and one untested. Thirteen relatives are WT/WT, ten negative for carriage and three untested.
limitations: Disease penetrance incomplete and age/exposure dependent; P4 is counted affected despite no positive Tw tissue/PCR confirmation. Shared-family linkage is not independent replication.

phase.statement: A single heterozygous IRF4 allele is described; no compound-heterozygous cis/trans question applies. Pedigree supports transmission from P3 to P1.

causal_confidence.statement: The authors attribute WD susceptibility in this family to R98W functional haploinsufficiency. Evidence combines family segregation, model-dependent linkage, private variant status at publication, impaired binding/transactivation in tested systems, and patient-cell findings. P1 infection is independently supported by positive synovial-fluid PCR/culture. This supports the source causal interpretation but is less absolute than packet SOLVED/CAUSATIVE/PATHOGENIC labels.

evidence.locator: Results and Discussion lines98-104; Figures1-6; full decision/response lines664-818

limitations: Single multiplex family; no second family and no IRF4 variant in25sporadic WD cases.
P4 arthralgia/serology case had negative saliva/fecal PCR and Tw not sought in joint fluid; its contribution to segregation is uncertain.
Healthy heterozygotes and an82-year-old healthy carrier show incomplete penetrance; another modifier locus explicitly not excluded.

Protein quantity is not halved: total/cytoplasmic accumulation with comparable nuclear levels; functional deficit is inferred from LOF and no dominant-negative effect in tested coexpression conditions.
Transcriptomic features were selected for response in at least4/6WT subjects before genotype comparison; clustering is not an independent unbiased diagnostic test. No raw GEO reanalysis.
No formal contemporary ACMG classification independently performed.

phenotype_completeness.statement: All five listed packet features have source correspondence, with synovial-lining hyperplasia mapped from MRI synovial hypertrophy rather than histology. Packet omits recurrent knee effusion, restricted movement, joint-space narrowing/erosion and organism detection. Normal ESR/CRP are explicit measurements during P1 workup.
limitations: MRI thickening does not itself demonstrate histologic hyperplasia.
Absence of raised inflammatory markers is encounter-specific, not a claim of lifelong normality.
Packet last-encounter age64 differs from source chronology.
Apparently normal immune development in prose must be qualified by source-data5 out-of-range subsets, including P1 naiveCD8 20% vs29-57 and central-memoryCD8 17% vs3-14.

assessment.statement: Source reports heterozygous IRF4 exon3 c.292C>T, p.Arg98Trp/R98W, with C/T Sanger trace for P1. Source-data Figure1-data2 row2 lists chr6:394896 C>T, numerically matching packet. Source resource transcript is NM_002460.3 and WES uses hg19; packet names NM_002460.4 and NC_000006.12/hg38.

evidence.locator: Figure1B-C; Results private heterozygous variant; Materials genome-wide analysis; key-resource table; Figure1-data2 row2

limitations: Coding/protein/zygosity and numeric position correspondence established; independent version/assembly normalization not performed.

assessment.statement: P1 ESR3mm/h is explicitly described as a negative determination, supporting the excluded abnormal-ESR feature.
P1 CRP1.8mg/l is explicitly described as a negative determination, supporting the excluded abnormal-CRP feature.
P1 arthralgia is explicitly reported to resolve after treatment; arthralgia is not being borrowed from P4.
Recurrent right-knee arthritis since1980 with a documented2011episode directly supports arthritis.
MRI showed right-knee synovial hypertrophy, corresponding clinically to the packet synovial-lining hyperplasia concept.
limitations: Source describes MRI hypertrophy; no synovial histology proving cellular hyperplasia is supplied.

Mandatory HANDOFF.md read at resume exposed aggregate benchmark outcomes and a historical HG002/FGFR2 public-control case-specific rank. Conservatively declared per_case; this old public-control exposure is distinct from target-case outcomes: no target-case inference/result files or additional outcome summaries were consulted for this review. This is post-inference source correspondence, not blinded validation. Earlier canonical reviews are inherited work and are not claimed as this reviewer reading.
This is newly personally read material. Saved predecessor canonical reviews retain their own attribution; none is claimed as reread here.
P1 identity is secure; age64 latest encounter conflicts with69 in source and2016follow-up. Arthritic onset1980 is distinct from diagnosis2011.

The four designated WD patients have unequal diagnostic evidence: P1 synovial PCR/culture positive, P2/P3 intestinal PAS positive, P4 serology and arthralgia without confirmed Tw in affected tissue. No new diagnosis is made.

Functional loss and abundance differ: R98W increases total/cytoplasmic protein while nuclear quantities are similar; nuclear WT fraction is inferred, not directly allele-specific measured. Reporter/EMSA findings apply to tested contexts.

Five truncating population alleles lack a C-terminal antibody signal; because the epitope is removed, this alone does not prove absence of truncated protein. Their functional LOF and intact expressed cDNA are separate evidence.

Other allele observations do not prove every IRF4 LOF causes WD: the HGID Gly279_His280del carrier was not a WD case and that allele did not segregate with the other family phenotype. c.403+2T>C and two noncanonical variants were unassayed; the workbook resolves missing plus sign in main prose c.4032T>C.

No-DN results cover the coexpression conditions shown, not all possible stoichiometries or cell types. Population-variant functional screen is predominantly ISRE reporter testing; apparent higher bars are not independently classified as gain of function.

Figure1-data2 has54variant rows but HYAL3 rs13100173 is duplicated in rows43/44; H46 is numeric38231 rather than a gene symbol, and values labelled MAF exceed0.5 in several rows. These defects do not alter the first-row IRF4 call but limit literal count/annotation reuse.

Figure1S1 rare filter shows MAF<1e-4 whereas prose excludes alternatives above1e-3. Source table alternatives are all above0.001, so the displayed difference does not change the listed candidate selection.

Pedigree IV.5 age70 does not align with1951birth date in Figure1-data1 under the other2017age labels; do not silently harmonize carrier ages. P1 age69 and DOB1948 fit2017, whereas narrative last follow-up is2016.

All156population/HGID variant rows, all54candidate rows, entire kindred table and193/29responsive-gene lists read. Responsive-gene lists provide probe IDs and direction, not per-person effect estimates; some probes map to more than one listed gene. WT-conditioned selection and small related cohorts limit interpretation.

Immune-cell development is described as apparently normal, yet source-data5 includes out-of-range values in patients and the healthy sister. Supplemental cytokine plots are small cohorts and are not proof of universally normal immunity.

Figure5supp6/7 short titles are inconsistent with their detailed captions/panels (naive/memory secretion versus polarization). The actual panels and captions were used. Reporting form source-data list1/3/5/6 differs from final linked1/2/5/6.

GEO GSE102862 is described, not downloaded or reanalyzed. This is complete reading of linked article components, not raw-data replication. All published methods were read solely to appraise evidence; no wet-lab design or execution.
